question.worked_solution:
The variable $x$ is being *divided* by $4.$ To isolate $x$ and remove the negative sign, we *multiply* by $-4$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}9\,\, & \ge \,\,-\frac{x}{4} \\ (-4)\cdot 9\,\, & \le \,\,(-4)\cdot (-\frac{x}{4}) \\ -36\,\, & \le \,\,(-4)\cdot (-\frac{x}{4})\end{aligned}
$$

Since two negative numbers multiply to give a positive number, we first cancel the negatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}-36\,\, & \le (-4)\cdot (-\frac{x}{4}) \\ -36 & \le (\cancel{-}4)\cdot (\cancel{-}\frac{x}{4}) \\ -36 & \le 4\cdot \frac{x}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel the common factor $4$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}-36 & \le 4\cdot \frac{x}{4} \\ -36 & \le \frac{4x}{4} \\ -36 & \le \frac{\cancel{4}x}{\cancel{4}} \\ -36 & \le x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the inequality with the variable on the left-hand side:

$$
x\ge -36
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x\ge -36.$
